questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had heard that Melbourne was supposed to be a great city to study in with a lot of opportunities and offers to students. Furthermore, I found the idea of travelling from Europe to the other side of the planet to study both really exciting and terrifying. Also, I liked that I would not be able to just go home if I felt homesick, so it seemed even more important to really create a connection to my study destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Jeg er virkelig enormt glad for, at jeg valgte at tage på udveksling. Det har været et helt fantastisk halvt år, hvor jeg er blevet udfordret både personligt og fagligt, men samtidig også haft det enormt sjovt og oplevet sindssygt meget. Det føles ret styrkende at vide med sig selv, at man tør rejse alene ud i verden for at studere og så skabe sig et hjem i et nyt land og møde nye mennesker og stille og roligt bygge et netværk op. Jeg er nærmest ked af, at jeg ikke var afsted i længere tid. Alt i alt vil jeg anbefale alle, der har en smule rejselyst eller nysgerrighed på udveskling, at tage afsted. Selvom det kan virke uoverskueligt eller skræmmende, så er det virkelig oplevelsen værd, og jeg erfarede også, at det hele flasker sig i sidste ende. Tag afsted!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The exchange team at Melbourne University was so great! They had all the information one would need and their communication worked as it should - there was not too much nor too little. I felt like I knew what to do, when to do it and how to do it. And if there was anything, you felt insecure about you could book appointments at uni and basically get any question answered.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received some assistance with my schedule for the subjects I wanted to take and choosing the right ones in regard to the pre-approval from my home institution.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It wasn't exactly easy, but I got quite lucky. I used a Facebook page called Fairy Floss Real Estate and a website called
flatmates.com
, and in the end, I found an apartment I could rent with a friend from this really nice, local lady. It was truly perfect, however the prizing in general was really high in Melbourne.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think it's important to consider that living off campus sometimes means that you have a certain amount of travel time from home to uni. On the other hand, it may be possible to save some money, and further, I found it really lovely living in the suburbs and in that way getting to know other neighbourhoods than just the one where uni is located. Also, I could bike to uni in 25 minutes and I thought it was a nice way to get to know the city and how the different parts of it are connected. I would definitely recommend living off campus if you feel like seeing and exploring other parts of the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think it was all a bit overwhelming containing a lot of information, but I was almost always able to find the answers I needed to complete the next step of the registration process.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration proces was divided into several steps, for instance applying for visa; completing necessary information; planning your subjects. Sometimes you had to wait a bit before you could move on to the next step but that was actually kind of nice, since it would have been a a lot to do it all at once.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The website of Melbourne University was really helpful in guiding me through the registration proces.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I managed to get most of the classes I wanted which was terrific.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have patience and trust the proces. I may seem a bit overwhelming at times but everything will work out and there's always help to get in case you feel unsure about something.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was positively surprised at the relatively high level of the courses, I took. It varied from first-year subjects to third-year but it worked pretty well having a mixture of these. I felt the ambitious level of some of the second- and third-year courses I had were specifically due to other students' engagement as well as the teacher's giant effort to make the courses exciting. I learned more than I had counted on from all my courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It has been quite different but a thing I really appreciated at Melbourne University was more academic freedom to write assignments within topics that I found interesting. Furthermore, I really enjoyed the amount of feedback we got which I found useful for my own academic development.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Understanding the Student as Learner (EDUC91029)
Science and Pseudoscience (HPSC10002)
The Politics of Sex (POLS20011)
Survey Design and Analysis (SOCI30013)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I highly recommend the course called The Politics of Sex as our lecturer, Lauren Rosewarne, was truly amazing at her job. The lectures were so interesting and I learned a ton from them, and as they were all recorded the course came with a great amount of flexibility. Furthermore, I found the seminars really exciting as we had a lot of great discussions on the topics from the lectures. Though the essays were challenging to write, they were also some of the most interesting.
Also, I would recommend Survey Design and Analysis to anyone who finds research within the social sciences interesting. Belinda and Shaun who taught the course were so nice and helpful and every topic from statistics and graphs to survey design and administration was explained thoroughly. Furthermore, the course was very "hands-on" as we got to actually design and distribute a real survey and then analyze the results as part of our final assignment.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I guess I was surprised at the cost of visa and insurance.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The rent was definitely more expensive than I'd counted on. Also, groceries were more expensive. However, coffee was cheap compared to home and that came in handy when you had long days at campus.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were so many different sports and social clubs at my host institution. I joined the Mountaineering Club and went on this amazing intro-trip for two straight days which was just really fun to try. Furthermore, it was a great way of meeting new people and other exchange students. Also, there was these really random, but fun clubs like a Taylor Swift Fan Society which I also joined.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would really recommend becoming a part of some sort of club as it is a great way to meet other people and make friends. Also, I recommend trying out free events at the university as there might be free food, great music or valuable information. Really, it almost doesn't matter what club you join as long as you find it interesting or you sense there's a good vibe there. Lastly, if you have the option to go on trips in your local area and around: do it! Explore the city and country and travel to see other parts of it.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I think you should strive to find a balance between going on trips and just setting aside time to relax and possibly catch up on studying. I loved having both weekends where I went on trips around Victoria State such as going to the Grampians, Great Ocean Road and Wilson's Prom but also the weekends spent at home in Melbourne just hanging out with friends or perhaps going to a local market or going for a walk along the river. Still, I really recommend using the holidays to go on longer trips or perhaps set aside some time after exams to travel. I managed to go to Tasmania over the Easter Break and that was truly wonderful.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it relatively easy as it reminded me of the culture of my homeland in many ways. It reflected the Western culture that dominates a lot of media and so on which I think made it quite familiar. In that sense, the culture shock wasn't too big. Still, the time zone and seasons were the total opposite from home so that was something to get used to upon arrival.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: My tip is to not be too shy. Say you have a nice chat with someone from your course, I would recommend just asking them if they'd like to grab a coffee or a beer sometime. I feel that most local students would definitely be up to that if you ask. You could also ask if they wanted to study or if they could help you explain some local phenomena that you struggle to understand, e.g. Australian Football which I did not get at all. Essentially, don't be scared of rejection as they are mostly really kind and helpful. Another way is joining clubs, and societies or going to uni events and just hang out.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don't know if it was really that challenging but I had to get used to everything being reversed in terms of traffic. Driving, walking, and biking on the left side. That was super strange in the beginning.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
I really find the history and traditions of the First Nation's People both interesting and tragic. I felt it was my responsibility to get to know some of this history as it also affected the culture. In Melbourne, I sensed a deep respect towards First Nations' history, however, it seemed it wasn't the same across the whole of Australia. In general, I think Melbourne was quite a long way ahead regarding political issues and debates on human rights, racism, LGBTQIA+ etc. 
On a more basic level, the food culture is great. Also, coffee and brunch. I also really enjoyed watching AFL games, and in general the sports and concert culture was also really great and had a lot to offer.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It's worth finding a nice place to live - possibly with nice housemates - as it will be your home every day for almost half a year. 
Also, don't be alarmed if you find the workload at uni heavy in the beginning as it takes some time to get used to the new study settings, classes taught in another language and different ways of writing assignments. And as marks don't transfer, you need only pass your courses to have them approved back home.
Lastly, remember to enjoy yourself and have fun but also reach out to people back home if you feel lonely or go through something difficult. Even if they are far away, they are still your family and friends and they can support you still.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think it's useful knowing that there are so many facilities offered that are worth exploring. Besides clubs and societies and free events, there are great study facilities and you can even apply for a food programme where you can be nominated to receive free dinners every week.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I'm really grateful for all the amazing people that I've met and got to share my experience with. I've gotten new friendships that I'm able to take home with me as well as a connection to another city that I now feel is also my home. The whole experience has been equally challenging and wonderful, and I wouldn't have been without any of it.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was feeling lonely at times and missing the feeling of being deeply connected to my friends and family back home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
